id: typescript-gateway-control-ui-insecure-auth-bypass
title: Control UI allowInsecureAuth config flag bypasses secure-context and device identity checks
summary: The gateway computes a Control UI bypass flag that includes the `allowInsecureAuth` config option
  alongside `dangerouslyDisableDeviceAuth`. A Control UI client could then connect with only a shared
  token or password over plain HTTP, with no device identity and no secure-context requirement. Anyone
  who obtains the token can authenticate from an insecure origin without a device-bound identity. The
  security audit also described this behaviour as intended, which is how the same mistake shows up in
  audit text.

- CWE-319
severity: high
confidence: medium

- typescript

  repository: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw
rule:
  message: 'Control UI bypass is derived from an "allow insecure auth" setting (or the audit text states
    that

    allowInsecureAuth permits token-only auth over HTTP and skips device identity). This lets

    token-only auth skip the secure-context/device identity requirement. Only the explicit dangerous

    device-auth-disable flag should bypass it.

    '
  pattern-either:
  - patterns:
    - pattern-either:
      - pattern: 'const $BYPASS = $INSECURE || $DISABLE;

          '
      - pattern: 'const $BYPASS = $DISABLE || $INSECURE;

          '
    - metavariable-regex:
        metavariable: $INSECURE
        regex: (?i).*allowInsecure.*
    - metavariable-regex:
        metavariable: $BYPASS
        regex: (?i).*(bypass|skipDevice|skipSecure).*
  - pattern-regex: allowInsecureAuth=true allows token-only auth over HTTP
fix:
  guidance: Do not let the legacy `allowInsecureAuth` setting influence the Control UI bypass decision.
    Derive the bypass solely from `dangerouslyDisableDeviceAuth`, so Control UI connections over insecure
    contexts without a device identity are rejected. Keep `allowInsecureAuth` only for compatibility and
    audit reporting, and make the audit text say that secure context and device identity are still enforced.
  example: '// allowInsecureAuth is retained for compatibility, but must not bypass

    // secure-context/device-auth requirements.

    const allowControlUiBypass = disableControlUiDeviceAuth;

    '
